In [[mathematics]], the '''extended natural numbers''' is a set which contains the values <math>0, 1, 2, \dots</math> and <math>\infty</math> (infinity). That is, it is the result of adding a [[greatest element|maximum element]] <math>\infty</math> to the [[natural number]]s. Addition and multiplication work as normal for finite values, and are extended by the rules <math>n+\infty=\infty+n=\infty</math> (<math>n\in\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}</math>), <math>0\times \infty=\infty \times 0=0</math> and <math>m\times \infty=\infty\times m=\infty</math> for <math>m\neq 0</math>.

With addition and multiplication, <math>\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}</math> is a [[semiring]] but not a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]], as <math>\infty</math> lacks an [[additive inverse]].{{sfnp|Sakarovitch|2009|p=28}} The set can be denoted by <math>\overline{\mathbb{N}}</math>, <math>\mathbb{N}_\infty</math> or <math>\mathbb{N}^\infty</math>.{{sfnp|Koch|2020}}{{sfnp|Escardó|2013}}{{sfnp|Khanjanzadeh|Madanshekaf|2018}} It is a subset of the [[extended real number line]], which extends the [[real number]]s by adding <math>-\infty</math> and <math>+\infty</math>.{{sfnp|Koch|2020}}

==Applications==
In [[graph theory]], the extended natural numbers are used to define distances in [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graphs]], with <math>\infty</math> being the distance between two [[connectivity (graph theory)|unconnected]] vertices.{{sfnp|Koch|2020}} They can be used to show the extension of some results, such as the [[max-flow min-cut theorem]], to infinite graphs.{{sfnp|Folkman|Fulkerson|1970}}

In [[topology]], the [[Grothendieck topos]] of right [[semigroup action|actions]] on the extended natural numbers is a [[Category (mathematics)|category]] '''PRO''' of [[Projective object|projection]] algebras.{{sfnp|Khanjanzadeh|Madanshekaf|2018}}

In [[constructive mathematics]], the extended natural numbers <math>\mathbb{N}_\infty</math> are a [[one-point compactification]] of the natural numbers, yielding the set of [[Sequence#Increasing and decreasing|non-increasing]] [[binary sequence]]s i.e. <math>(x_0,x_1,\dots)\in 2^\mathbb{N}</math> such that <math>\forall i\in\mathbb{N}: x_i\ge x_{i+1}</math>. The sequence <math>1^n 0^\omega</math> represents <math>n</math>, while the sequence <math>1^\omega</math> represents <math>\infty</math>. It is a [[Retraction (topology)|retract]] of <math>2^\mathbb{N}</math> and the claim that <math>\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}\subseteq \mathbb{N}_\infty</math> implies the [[limited principle of omniscience]].{{sfnp|Escardó|2013}}
